correctness.rationale: For the 12 regular icosahedron vertices and normalized 9-dimensional spherical harmonics up to degree 2, exact fourth moments give U*U=I_9. The row projection kernel is (1+3t+5P_2(t))/12, giving diagonal 3/4, antipodal 1/4, and all other off-diagonal ±1/(4 sqrt5). After erasing E the retained Gram matrix is I_9−U_E*U_E, whose nonunit eigenvalues are one minus those of the |E|×|E| kernel. Explicit 1-, 2- and 3-point matrix diagonalizations give the claimed spectra; an antipodal pair forces eigenvalue one in the erased kernel. For any |E|>=4 there are <=8 retained observations, so rank 9 is impossible. Counting antipodal pairs gives 1,12,60,160 successful masks. Six vertex axes give an equiangular tight frame with Seidel spectrum ±sqrt5 threefold, hence trace(S^3)=0 and exactly 10 positive and 10 negative axis triples, or 80 each among 160 signed triples. The minimum good squared singular value is 1/4−1/(2 sqrt5), attained at 80 positive triples. Independently built the 12×9 numerical frame and directly checked the full small-erasure kernel/eigenvalue census (299 masks), all 233 good masks and the 80/80 split; the exact 5-design and Seidel arguments prove this exhaustively.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General design quadrature implies U*U=I and frame-complement formulas reduce the problem to erased row Gram matrices; neither by itself gives the signed icosahedral triple classification and exact worst good eigenvalue. Cuboctahedron has distinct node geometry, so its results are not a dominating icosahedral parameter family.
